plan.title: Immune/stromal deconvolution of anti-PD-1 melanoma TPM data
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12,000 genes x 12 samples: 6 anti-PD-1 treated vs 6 untreated melanoma biopsies, unpaired, single batch) with no raw counts or quant directories, and sample_01 sequenced at ~1/4 median depth. Because raw counts are unavailable, count-based tools (CIBERSORTx via counts, DESeq2) are out of scope; the plan uses TPM-native methods throughout, per the knowledge service's grounded procedure for bulk RNA-seq deconvolution from TPM. Track 1 does sample-structure QC on log2(TPM+1) (flagging, not silently dropping, the low-depth sample), then filters low-abundance genes with a TPM floor scaled to this design's smallest group (n=6). Track 2 estimates immune/stromal composition with four TPM-compatible, complementary methods run through immunedeconv where possible: EPIC and quanTIseq for absolute cell fractions (with EPIC's uncharacterized/tumor fraction), MCP-counter for abundance scores of a broader stromal+immune panel, and xCell for 64 fine-grained cell types with spillover compensation. CIBERSORT/CIBERSORTx (LM22, the conventional tool of record) and ESTIMATE (tumor purity) are licensed/absent from this environment and are explicitly not substituted silently — the report states this gap. Track 3 tests each cell-type estimate for a treated-vs-control difference (nonparametric, given n=6/group and non-normal compositional scores) with BH correction, and requires agreement across ≥2 deconvolution methods before any compositional claim is called robust, per the grounded consensus rule. A final integration step reports per-sample composition, the treated-vs-control differences, method agreement, and the caveats (TPM-only input, sample_01 depth, no LM22/ESTIMATE equivalent).

Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.
